standard.title: Effects of colonisation on First Nations Australians
standard.description: the effects of contact with other people on First Nations Australians and their Countries/Places following the arrival of the First Fleet and how this was viewed by First Nations Australians as an invasion
standard.prior_knowledge: From AC9HS4K01-K03: Students have explored First Nations Australian diversity and First Fleet establishment. They now examine contact from First Nations Australian perspectives.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students explain the effects of contact following 1788 on First Nations Australians, including how colonisation was experienced as an invasion.

nodes.label: Contact before 1788
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe contact between First Nations Australians and people from Asia and Europe before 1788, including trade and conflict.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least one example of contact between First Nations Australians and non-British visitors before 1788.
nodes.typical_width: Investigate contact between First Nations Australians and people from different continents (Asia, Europe) before 1788; examine examples of trade, sharing of ideas and technologies; explore the repulsion of the Dutch at Cape Keerweer (1606).
wider: Compare First Nations Australian interactions with Macassans and with early European visitors, noting differences in the nature of contact
Investigate rock paintings depicting contact with Macassans and discuss what these reveal from a First Nations perspective
nodes.hinge_reason: Establishing that First Nations Australians had prior agency in contact situations provides essential context for understanding the qualitative shift that British colonisation represented.

response_modes.reason: Pre-1788 agency must be established explicitly or students will naturalise colonial disruption as inevitable — this counter-narrative framing requires conscious scaffolding.

success_criteria: Describes at least one example of pre-1788 contact between First Nations Australians and non-British visitors
Identifies the nature of that contact (e.g. trade, conflict, exchange)

nodes.label: Effects of colonisation — perspectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can describe the effects of British colonisation on First Nations Australians (dispossession, disease, frontier conflict, dislocation, loss of food sources) and explain how colonisation was experienced as an invasion.
nodes.minimum_width: Describe at least two effects of colonisation on First Nations Australians and explain why colonisation was experienced as an invasion.
nodes.typical_width: Examine paintings and accounts to explore impact of British colonisation on First Nations Australians; describe dispossession, dislocation, loss of lives, disease, loss of food sources and medicines; consider differing perspectives of interactions; explain the invasion perspective.
wider: Research the perspectives of specific First Nations Australian individuals (Pemulwuy, Windradyne, Bennelong) on early colonial contact
Examine paintings and compare what European and First Nations Australian accounts reveal about the same events

response_modes.reason: Multiple First Nations Australian voices and experiences give richer understanding of colonisation's effects than a single narrative.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The invasion perspective is central to Australian historical literacy — engaging with multiple First Nations Australian accounts deepens rather than simplifies this complex topic.
success_criteria: Describes at least two effects of colonisation on First Nations Australians
Explains why colonisation was experienced as an invasion from a First Nations perspective
